narrative:
Your loan application was carefully reviewed, and the assessment found a 63% likelihood that you represent a credit risk — a level of uncertainty high enough that the application could not be approved at this time. This decision was not made lightly, and understanding the specific factors behind it may help you take steps toward a stronger application in the future.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, your lack of significant property assets, and the length of the loan you requested. Together, these three elements painted a picture of financial vulnerability that the model weighed heavily against approval.

Starting with your checking account, having a balance in the 0–200 DM range was the single most influential factor pushing toward a denial. Among applicants who were approved, the largest group — about half — had no checking account linked to the application at all, while only around 23% shared your account status. A low or borderline checking account balance signals limited financial cushion, which raises concerns about your ability to handle unexpected expenses during the repayment period.

Your property situation also worked against you in a meaningful way. You currently have no registered property — no real estate, no vehicle, no life insurance or savings plan that could serve as a financial safety net. Among approved applicants, nearly 88% held some form of property, with real estate and vehicles being the most common. The absence of any such asset means there is little to fall back on if your financial situation were to change, which the model interpreted as an added layer of risk.

The duration of the loan you requested — 36 months — was the third most influential factor. The average approved applicant requested credit for just over 19 months, meaning your requested term is nearly twice as long. A longer loan period increases the window during which financial circumstances can shift, and combined with the other concerns, this extended timeline added to the overall risk assessment.

It is worth noting that several aspects of your profile are genuinely positive: you are employed in a management or highly skilled role, you own your home, you have no other debtors or co-signers complicating the picture, and your credit history shows existing debts being paid — all characteristics shared with many approved applicants. These strengths were not ignored, but they were not sufficient to outweigh the combination of a low checking balance, no property assets, and a lengthy repayment term.

As a next step, you may want to consider applying for a shorter loan duration or a smaller amount, as the 4,795 DM you requested is also notably higher than the approved applicant average of around 2,887 DM. Building up savings or acquiring a registered asset before reapplying could also significantly improve your standing. Speaking with a financial advisor or a bank representative directly could help you identify the most practical path forward given your specific circumstances.
